visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) A young girl with pigtails, wearing a red sleeveless t-shirt with a watermelon print and beige shorts, crawls across a light-colored wooden floor in a modern living room. The lighting is bright and natural, coming from a large window in the background. (2) She stops crawling and picks up a large, realistic grey T-Rex toy, holding it with both hands. She looks at the toy with an excited expression, her mouth slightly open. (3) The scene shifts to the girl standing, holding the dinosaur toy up to her chest. She mimics an eating motion with the toy, pushing its head forward. In the background, white bookshelves filled with colorful children's books and toys are visible. (4) She walks over to a white bean bag where an adult with a tattooed arm is resting. She presses the dinosaur's mouth against the adult's leg, pretending the toy is biting them. (5) The girl stands in the middle of the room, curling her fingers like claws and opening her mouth wide to imitate a dinosaur's roar. She looks directly at the camera with a playful and energetic expression. (6) A final title card appears with a pink background and a cartoon illustration of the girl, featuring branding text.

audio_base.audio_narrative_log: (1) The audio begins with a bouncy, light-hearted pizzicato-style electronic melody. A high-pitched child's voice emits playful, rhythmic breathing sounds as if mimicking a small animal. (2) A sharp 'clack' sound indicates the toy dinosaur hitting the floor. A male voice speaks with a gentle, teasing tone, followed by the child's joyful squeal. (3) The background music maintains a consistent tempo. A female voice enters, laughing warmly and encouraging the child. The child's vocal intensity increases as she makes growling noises. (4) Multiple layers of laughter and quick dialogue exchanges occur. Every few seconds, subtle cartoon-like popping or 'ding' sound effects are inserted during scene transitions. (5) The child performs a sustained, high-arousal growl imitation. The male and female voices react with exaggerated tones of mock-fear. (6) The music swells slightly in volume for the final five seconds as the child continues to make playful dinosaur noises until a final hard cut.
